Borrowers may need to pledge additional collateral or repay debts as their gold loans become inadequately backed. Encounters of repayment stress are already visible among major lenders such as IIFL Finance and Bajaj Finance.

articles.title: India's FY28 fiscal deficit projected to stay unchanged at 4.3% of GDP: Deutsche Bank
articles.desc: India's fiscal deficit for the financial year 2028 is expected to stay at 4.3 percent of GDP. The report highlights challenges in consolidation efforts due to rising expenditure and subsidy bills. Economic growth remains steady, with GDP forecasts at 7.3 percent for FY27 and 7.2 percent for FY28. Retail inflation surpassed the RBI's upper threshold driven primarily by higher food prices.

articles.title: Dollar set for weekly gain as risk appetite returns
articles.desc: The Australian dollar and other risk-sensitive currencies strengthened on Friday, buoyed by a positive shift in market sentiment. The US dollar also noted slight gains for the week amid ongoing volatility in equity markets. Anticipation surrounding future Federal Reserve rate hikes has influenced currency dynamics, while the dollar climbed against the Japanese yen amidst worries over intervention and rising inflation in Tokyo.

articles.title: European shares log strong weekly gains; markets await Spanish election

The outcome may not only impact Spain but also ripple into crucial elections in France and Italy.

articles.desc: India's unincorporated MSME sector is witnessing faster productivity growth and narrowing regional disparities, with manufacturing recording the biggest gains, according to four rounds of ASUSE data. articles.title: OPEC+ set to keep oil production targets steady: Report
articles.desc: OPEC+ is expected to maintain its production targets for Q1 2027, despite complexities arising from conflicting member production estimates and the ongoing Iran conflict. As the group reassesses its capacity data, some members voice their concerns over the initial findings. Analysts foresee a potential global oil surplus next year, increasing pressure on OPEC+, further complicated by recent exits of nations like the United Arab Emirates and Angola, indicating internal frictions.

articles.title: Copper sweeps higher as China offers stock market support
articles.desc: Copper prices experienced a notable increase after China's cabinet announced its support for the stock market, which positively impacted global equities. The Yangshan premium for copper reflects a robust demand for imports, even in the face of recent downturns.

The stake sale was necessary to comply with minimum public shareholding requirements under Sebi regulations. Following the sale, shares of International Gemological Institute rose by 1.
